title: When Do LLMs Model the Right Target? Problem Formulation in High-Stakes Risk Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.23638v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used to assist with data science tasks, yet fundamental questions remain about its ability to correctly formulate analytical problems. We investigate how well large language models (LLMs) can formulate prediction problems when developing models for high-stakes decision making. We focus on one particular challenge to validity: decision dependency, which arises when historical decisions affect observed outcomes. We evaluate this aspect of problem formulation in LLM-generated code and explanations across child-welfare, healthcare, and employment settings, using 11 models from OpenAI and Anthropic and seven prompt conditions. We assess whether the LLM-generated code implements a procedure appropriate for estimating the intended outcome under the study's assumptions and whether the explanation acknowledges decision dependency. translated_title: 大型语言模型何时能建模正确的目标？高风险风险预测中的问题构建
translated_abstract: 生成式AI正日益被用于辅助数据科学任务，但其正确构建分析问题的能力仍存在根本性的疑问。我们研究了大型语言模型在为高风险决策制定开发模型时，能够多好地构建预测问题。我们专注于效度面临的一个特定挑战：决策依赖性，即历史决策会影响观察到的结果。我们在儿童福利、医疗保健和就业场景中，使用来自OpenAI和Anthropic的11个模型以及七种提示条件，评估LLM生成的代码和解释中问题构建的这一方面。我们评估LLM生成的代码是否实现了在研究假设下适合估计预期结果的程序，以及其解释是否承认决策依赖性。我们发现，在没有指导的情况下，LLM无法可靠地解决决策依赖性问题。
tldr: 该研究通过儿童福利、医疗保健和就业三大高风险场景的实验评估发现，在缺乏明确指导的情况下，LLM在构建风险预测问题时无法可靠地识别和处理“决策依赖性”（即历史决策影响观察结果的效度威胁），凸显了将LLM用于高风险决策建模时人工审查问题构建的必要性。
en_tdlr: LLMs do not reliably account for decision dependency—where historical decisions affect observed outcomes—when formulating high-stakes risk prediction problems across child-welfare, healthcare, and employment settings without explicit guidance.
